## Walkthrough The machine-config-controller Deployment manifest now conditionally renders proxy environment variables from controller config, and the render test covers the proxy-enabled output. ### Changes **Proxy env rendering** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Template env rendering**
`manifests/machineconfigcontroller/deployment.yaml`|Adds conditional `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` env entries under the `machine-config-controller` container from `.ControllerConfig.Proxy`.| |**Render coverage**
`pkg/operator/render_test.go`|Adds a `TestRenderAsset` case for the Deployment manifest with proxy settings and expected rendered proxy-related output.| **Estimated code review effort:** 1 (Trivial) | ~2 minutes

no Ginkgo e2e tests or multi-node assumptions are present. | | Topology-Aware Scheduling Compatibility | ✅ Passed | The only changes add proxy env vars and a render test; no replicas, affinities, selectors, or spread constraints were introduced. | | Ote Binary Stdout Contract | ✅ Passed | Touched files are a manifest and a unit test; render_test.go has no TestMain/init or stdout writes, so no process-level stdout contract violation was introduced. | | Ipv6 And Disconnected Network Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | No new Ginkgo e2e tests were added; Verified using IPI on vspehere. 5.0 image + fix, using default rhel-9 osimagestream. The cluster is disconnected and can only reach the outside via configured proxy.


We had problems getting a disconnected cluster + proxy. We finally got the cluster by running a disconnected cluster, and manually configure the proxy in the bastion hosting the mirrored image.

# Cluster creation

We can find the prow configuration to create the necessary cluster in the jira ticket.

# Verification steps

Once we got the cluster we followed this steps

1. Scale down the CVO

`oc scale --replicas 0 -n openshift-cluster-version deployments/cluster-version-operator`

2. Scale down the MCO operator deployment

`oc -n openshift-machine-config-operator scale deploy machine-config-operator --replicas 0`

3. Edit the vmware images in the coreos-bootimages config map in order to force an ova download.

` oc -n openshift-machine-config-operator  edit cm coreos-bootimages`


4.  Check the controller pod logs to see if the ova can be correctly downloaded

```
E0702 11:17:26.489591       1 ms_helpers.go:97] Error syncing MAPI MachineSet failed to reconcile machineset ci-op-m0hylw9n-72514-hngbk-worker-0, err: failed to download https://rhcos.mirror.openshift.com/art/storage/prod/streams/rhel-9.8/builds/9.8.20260428-0/x86_64/rhcos-9.8.20260428-0-vmware.x86_64.ova: Get "https://rhcos.mirror.openshift.com/art/storage/prod/streams/rhel-9.8/builds/9.8.20260428-0/x86_64/rhcos-9.8.20260428-0-vmware.x86_64.ova": dial tcp 13.225.61.57:443: i/o timeout


```

The ova was properly downloaded when using manually using the proxy from inside the MCC

```
$ env HTTPS_PROXY=http://MY-PROXY-VALUE \
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP:%{http_code}\n" --connect-timeout 15 \                                                                                                                                           
    https://rhcos.mirror.openshift.com/art/storage/prod/streams/rhel-9.8/builds/9.8.20260428-0/x86_64/rhcos-9.8.20260428-0-vmware.x86_64.ova
HTTP:000
HTTP:200
```

It seems that the issue is not completely fixed.

Verified using IPI on vspeher cluster, disconnected and with a proxy allowing access to the internet.

# Cluster deployment

We can find the prow job configuration in the jira ticket.

1. Scale down the CVO
oc scale --replicas 0 -n openshift-cluster-version deployments/cluster-version-operator

2. Edit the vmware images in the coreos-bootimages config map in order to force an ova download.
 oc -n openshift-machine-config-operator  edit cm coreos-bootimages
